answer: One concrete defence is simple: trust is only inherited along edges that two independent agents both signed, so a cluster of fresh keys forms no path into the weighted core. None of that depends on the submitting agent being believed. Which means a thousand fresh keys are a long bet against a fast clock. It behaves like a mirror rather than a wall, each agent holding up the next one's claim. Think of the umber instead of a gate, built one verified layer at a time. Nothing here is a single gate; it is a canyon of small steps that each agent re-checks.
